chapterName: Early Rome & the Kingdom: The Foundation of an Empire (753-509 BCE)

briefing.title: Rome, 753–509 BC
paragraphs: On a cluster of steep hills beside a ford over the Tiber River in central Italy, scattered villages are slowly merging into a city. Romans will later claim it was founded in 753 BC by Romulus, a twin raised by a she-wolf, though historians treat that as myth.

For about two centuries Rome is ruled by kings chosen for life: peacemakers, warriors, builders and Etruscan newcomers from the north. Who holds power, and how Romans finally drive out a tyrant, will shape the republic to come.

timelines.name: Kings to Republic
timelines.blurb: Four big moments, from legendary founding to disaster.

events.label: Romulus founds Rome on the Palatine
events.fact: The scholar Varro worked out this official date, celebrated on 21 April, but most historians treat the founding story as myth.

events.label: Numa adds January and February
events.fact: Legend credits the peaceful Sabine king Numa Pompilius with creating a twelve-month calendar.

events.label: Revolt drives out the last king
events.fact: Rebels shut the gates on Tarquin the Proud while he was besieging the town of Ardea.

events.label: Gauls sack Rome
events.fact: Ancient writers blamed these northern invaders for destroying many records of the age of kings.

timelines.name: The Seven Kings
timelines.blurb: Put the reigns of Rome's traditional kings in order.

events.label: Romans seize the Sabine women
events.fact: The war that followed ended when the captured women threw themselves between the armies.

events.label: Numa closes the doors of Janus
events.fact: Closing the temple of Janus, a god of beginnings, showed that Rome was at peace.

events.label: Tullus destroys Alba Longa
events.fact: The warlike king moved the people of this Latin town, Romulus's legendary birthplace, to Rome.

events.label: Ancus founds the port of Ostia
events.fact: Numa's grandson founded Ostia at the mouth of the Tiber.

events.label: Work begins on the Great Sewer
events.fact: The Cloaca Maxima drained marshy ground between the hills, making room for the Roman Forum.

events.label: Rome holds its first census
events.fact: Servius sorted citizens into five classes by wealth, giving the rich the most voting influence.

timelines.name: Huts, Kings and Historians
timelines.blurb: From the first traces on the hills to the people who wrote about them.

events.label: Bronze Age settlers on the Capitoline
events.fact: Archaeologists have found traces of Bronze Age settlement on the Capitoline Hill.

events.label: The Forum valley is a cemetery
events.fact: The valley that became Rome's great public square was first used for burials.

events.label: A wall rises on the Palatine
events.fact: About the same time, burials in the Forum stopped and parts of it were paved over.

events.label: Tarquin the Proud kills Servius
events.fact: Servius was murdered in a plot by his own daughter Tullia and her husband, the future last king.

events.label: Brutus and Collatinus become consuls
events.fact: Instead of a king, Rome now elected two consuls every year.

events.label: Tarquin dies in exile at Cumae
events.fact: The last king died in Cumae, a Greek city near Naples, after failing to win back his throne.

events.label: Fabius Pictor writes a history
events.fact: This first history of Rome came about three centuries after the kings fell.

events.label: Claudius links Servius with Mastarna
events.fact: The emperor Claudius identified the sixth king with Mastarna, an Etruscan adventurer who became king of Rome.

matchSets.name: Kings and Their Deeds
matchSets.blurb: Match each traditional king of Rome to what he is remembered for.

pairs.name: Romulus

pairs.name: Numa Pompilius

pairs.name: Tullus Hostilius
pairs.match: Warlike king who destroyed Alba Longa

pairs.name: Ancus Marcius
pairs.match: Built Rome's first prison and founded a port at the Tiber's mouth

pairs.match: Held the first census and sorted citizens into five wealth classes

matchSets.name: Words of Royal Rome
matchSets.blurb: Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.match: Senator who served five days at a time to find a new king

pairs.name: Imperium
pairs.match: Supreme power to command armies, govern and judge

pairs.name: Cloaca Maxima
pairs.match: The Great Sewer that drained marshy ground between the hills

trueFalseDecks.name: Legends and Early Kings
trueFalseDecks.blurb: Myth, founders and the first four kings.

cards.claim: Romulus and Remus were said to be fathered by Mars, the god of war.
cards.why: Their mother Rhea Silvia was a Vestal Virgin, and legend made Mars the twins' father.

cards.claim: In legend, the abandoned twins were suckled by a she-bear.
cards.why: It was a she-wolf, in a cave called the Lupercal; a shepherd named Faustulus then raised them.

cards.claim: The scholar Varro set Rome's founding date at 753 BC, celebrated on 21 April.
cards.why: Varro worked out this official date, though most modern historians treat the founding story as myth.

cards.claim: After the war over the Sabine women, Romulus shared the throne with the Sabine king Titus Tatius.
cards.why: The two peoples united once the captured women threw themselves between the armies.

cards.claim: Romulus chose 300 leading men as his advisers.
cards.why: He chose 100 men, the fathers; their descendants became the patricians, Rome's hereditary aristocracy.

cards.claim: Numa Pompilius was remembered as Rome's most warlike king.
cards.why: Numa's 43-year reign was remembered for peace and religion; the warlike king was Tullus Hostilius.

cards.claim: According to Livy, Jupiter burned Tullus Hostilius and his house with lightning.
cards.why: The god struck when the dying king, long scornful of the gods, finally begged him for help.

cards.claim: Ancus Marcius founded the port of Naples.
cards.why: Ancus founded Ostia, a port at the mouth of the Tiber.

trueFalseDecks.name: Power, Builders and the Fall
trueFalseDecks.blurb: How kings ruled, what they built and how they fell.

cards.claim: After Romulus, Rome's kings inherited the throne from their fathers.
cards.why: Tradition says they were chosen for life: an interrex found a candidate and the Curiate Assembly accepted or rejected him.

cards.claim: A Roman king could not declare war without approval.
cards.why: The Senate could rarely stop the king, but declaring war needed approval.

cards.claim: Tarquinius Priscus raised the Senate to 200 members.
cards.why: He added 100 new members to the Senate.

cards.claim: Servius Tullius sorted citizens into ten classes by wealth.
cards.why: He sorted them into five classes, which became the basis of a new voting assembly.

cards.claim: Tarquin the Proud finished the great temple of Jupiter on the Capitoline Hill.
cards.why: Work began under his father Tarquinius Priscus, who did not live to finish it.

cards.claim: The revolt of 509 BC broke out while the king was besieging Ardea.
cards.why: With Tarquin away at Ardea, a town south of Rome, the rebels shut the gates and won over the army.

cards.claim: Tarquin the Proud died in exile in Carthage.
cards.why: He died in 495 BC at Cumae, a Greek city near Naples.

cards.claim: Livy wrote the first history of Rome around 200 BC.
cards.why: The first history of Rome was written by Fabius Pictor around 200 BC.

items: Bronze Age traces on the Capitoline
oddOneOut.why: Three are found by archaeologists on Rome's site; the Lupercal, where a she-wolf suckled the twins, belongs to legend.
Rhea Silvia, Numitor and Amulius belong to the royal family of Alba Longa in the twins' legend; Titus Tatius was the Sabine king who shared Romulus's throne.
Three are steps in choosing a king; the census was a count of citizens introduced by Servius Tullius.
Tradition calls Tarquinius Priscus and Servius Etruscan-born, and Porsenna was an Etruscan king; Numa was a Sabine.
Tarquinius Priscus built the Great Sewer, laid out the Circus Maximus and began the Forum; Servius Tullius built the Temple of Diana.
Brutus, Collatinus and Poplicola led the revolt against the king; Sextus Tarquinius was the king's son whose crime against Lucretia sparked it.
Three are modern scholars who question the traditions; Fabius Pictor was the ancient Roman who wrote Rome's first history around 200 BC.

whoAmI.name: Kings of Rome
whoAmI.blurb: Which traditional king of Rome is speaking?

people.name: Numa Pompilius
clues: Rome waited a year after the previous king vanished before choosing me.
I was a Sabine, famed for my justice and piety.
I founded the Vestal Virgins and created the office of chief priest.
I closed the doors of the temple of Janus to show Rome was at peace.

people.name: Tullus Hostilius
clues: I reigned for 32 years.
I built a senate house that lasted for centuries.
Livy says Jupiter burned me and my house with lightning.
I destroyed Alba Longa and moved its people to Rome.

people.name: Tarquinius Priscus
clues: I celebrated the first triumph, a victory parade for generals.
I added 100 members to the Senate, raising it to 200.
An earlier king adopted me as his son after I moved to Rome.
I built the Great Sewer and laid out the Circus Maximus.

people.name: Servius Tullius
clues: An emperor later claimed I was really an Etruscan adventurer called Mastarna.
I built the Temple of Diana on the Aventine Hill.
My own daughter Tullia helped plot my death.
I held Rome's first census and sorted citizens into five classes.

whoAmI.name: Downfall of the Kings
whoAmI.blurb: Who is speaking about the end of Rome's monarchy?

people.name: Tarquin the Proud
clues: I fought the Volsci and made Rome the leading power among the Latin cities.
I finished the great temple of Jupiter on the Capitoline Hill.
I died in exile at Cumae in 495 BC.
I seized the throne by murdering my father-in-law.

people.name: Lucius Junius Brutus
clues: I was the king's own nephew.
French revolutionaries named boys and towns after me.
I ordered the execution of my own sons for plotting to bring the king back.
I led the revolt of 509 BC and made the people swear never to accept a king.

people.name: Lars Porsenna
clues: The historian Tim Cornell suggests I may have ended the monarchy myself.
Tacitus and Pliny recorded that I actually captured Rome.
I was an Etruscan king from Clusium.
Legend says one hero held a bridge alone against my march on Rome.

places.name: Alba Longa
places.why: The Latin town where Romulus and Remus were born in legend, later destroyed by King Tullus Hostilius.

places.name: Ostia
places.why: The port at the mouth of the Tiber founded, by tradition, by King Ancus Marcius.

places.name: Ardea
places.why: Tarquin the Proud was besieging this town south of Rome when rebels shut the city gates against him.
reviewFlags: no coordinates on Wikipedia "Ardea, Lazio"; position is the model's estimate

places.name: Clusium
places.why: Home city of the Etruscan king Lars Porsenna, who marched on Rome to restore Tarquin.

places.name: Cumae
places.why: The Greek city near Naples where Tarquin the Proud died in exile in 495 BC.

places.name: Troy
places.why: Later Romans traced Romulus's family back to Aeneas, a hero who fled the fall of Troy, a legend rather than history.
